Given `mode="tick"` and any plan, line 99 calls `log.append("session.note", ...)`, so the audit trail is a session note, not a dispatch.planned event, and a consumer looking for that kind never sees the advice.

chunk_findings.detail: `_render` treats steer results as dicts while the caller treats them as objects. `data["moves"]` is built with `m.verb` / `m.lane` / `m.text`, then `_render(rows, moves)` does `m["verb"]` and `m["lane"]`. Any non-empty steer list (a stalled lane that should surface as RESUME) raises TypeError in one of those two accesses, so the plan is not returned.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/dispatch.py:105

chunk_findings.detail: The start rows drop the fields the planner is required to return. Rows are only `item`, `lane`, `globs`, `note`. With 3 free slots and 5 ready items the response still has no agent name, claim command, rendered launch brief, or pin-file rule, so an operator cannot start the advised items from this result.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/dispatch.py:86

chunk_findings.detail: `Plan.free` is documented as the free slots the fill consumed, but `plan` stores the caller’s raw `free` and ignores what `fill` actually accepted. Given `free=-1`, `fill` clamps to 0 and returns no starts, yet `Plan.free` is `-1`. Given `free=3` and only one eligible item, `starts` has length 1 while `Plan.free` is still 3, so a caller that treats `free` as slots taken over-counts capacity.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/dispatch/plan.py:157

chunk_findings.detail: `steer` keeps only `m.lanes[0]`. A stall or over-limit move that names more than one lane drops the rest: `Move(kind="stall", lanes=("a", "b"), text="stuck")` becomes a single `NUDGE` for `"a"`, and `"b"` is never steered. An in-vocabulary move with `lanes=()` becomes `RESUME`/`NUDGE`/`YIELD` on `""`, which is not a lane.

chunk_findings.detail: Scenario 1 is entirely sequential: `_release`, `next`, `claim` T2, then `queue run`. chunk_findings.detail: The suite is supposed to block on `rp.parent / "hold"`, but that path is never passed on the command line or in the environment, and nothing in this change reads it. `queue run` can finish and drop `MQ.holder` before the 50 ms poll sees it, so `assert MQ.holder(rp)` fails even when the lease was already released; the “lease gone while waiting” check is a race, not a held lock.
